cognate: Gk ὄφις = Ved. áhi- = Av. aži- < *h₁ógʷʰis (object noun); Ved. han- / Av. jan- < *gʷʰen- (verb)
drift_or_renewal: renewal: Greek replaces *gʷʰen- (θείνω, πέφνον, φόνος) by κτείνω in the dragon-killing sentence; the object noun stays cognate
shared_syntax: transitive aorist 'slew' + accusative singular of the serpent noun, hero as subject (κτεῖνε ... ὄφιν ~ ahann ahiṃ)
context: Pindar's Jason slays the guardian serpent with his skill; AVŚ 2.5.11 (= RV 1.32.2) Indra slays the serpent lying on the mountain. Same mythic deed (hero kills serpent), same clause shape; Avestan janat̰ ažīm (Y 9.8, 9.11, Thraetaona) gives a third branch with the verb still cognate
phrase: *gʷʰent h₁ógʷʰim 'slew the serpent' (Gk with renewed verb)

cognate: Gk Ζεύς/Διί = Ved. dyáuḥ = Lat. Iu- (Iupiter) < *dyḗws; Gk πατήρ = Ved. pitā́ = Lat. -piter < *ph₂tḗr
drift_or_renewal: none (Latin has fused the vocative phrase *dyeu ph₂ter into the theonym Iupiter)
shared_syntax: theonym + appositional 'father' (Ζεὺς πατήρ / Διὶ πατρί ~ dyaúṣ pitā́; fused in Iu-piter)
context: The sky god addressed or named as father: HyAphr 29 and HyAp 307 of Zeus; AVŚ 6.120.4, 2.28.7, 9.10.23 Heaven as father (paired with Earth as mother); Cato's prayer to Iupiter dapalis. Three branches, same divine name + same kin title

cognate: Gk εὐρύς = Ved. urú- < *h₁wérHus; Gk πόντος = Ved. pánthā-/path- < *póntoh₁s
drift_or_renewal: drift: *póntoh₁s 'path, passage' became 'sea' in Greek (the sea as the path one crosses; cf. Pindar's πόντου κελεύθους, Homeric ὑγρὰ κέλευθα), while Vedic keeps 'path'; the adjective is unchanged
shared_syntax: attributive adjective + noun, same order and case-agreement (εὐρέα πόντον acc. ~ urúm pánthām acc.; εὐρέι πόντῳ ~ uraú pathí loc./pathā́ urúṇā instr.)
context: Greek: travelling/sailing over or being cast into the broad sea (Hes. WD 650 ἐπέπλων εὐρέα πόντον); Vedic: the broad path along which gods, chariots or the dakṣiṇā travel. In both the phrase names a route traversed. Corpus counts: 9 of 134 Homeric πόντος lines carry εὐρύς (~11x chance); 5 of 154 RV pánthā- padas carry urú- (~8x chance), so it is a collocation in each tradition, not a one-off

cognate: Gk ἄμβροτος = Ved. amṛ́ta- < *n̥-mr̥-tó-; Gk ἕννυμι/ἕσσαν, εἷμα = Ved. vas- 'clothe' < *wes-
drift_or_renewal: Vedic uses the substantivized neuter amṛ́tam ('the immortal', ambrosia) as the garment itself (instr./acc.), Greek puts ἄμβροτος on the garment noun (εἵματα, itself *wes-men-); Greek also has the substantive ἀμβροσίη alongside in Il. 16.670/680
shared_syntax: verb *wes- 'clothe' with the 'immortal' as what is put on (περὶ δ’ ἄμβροτα εἵματα ἕσσαν ~ amṛ́tena ánu vastām; amṛtam vasānām 'wearing the immortal')
context: Divine protection of a body: HyAphr 6 the Horai dress Aphrodite; Il. 16.670-80 Sarpedon's corpse anointed with ambrosia and dressed in immortal garments; RV 6.75.18 (= AVŚ 7.118.1) armour charm, 'let king Soma clothe you with the immortal'; AVŚ 9.1.2 the honey-whip 'wearing the immortal'. Same verb root, same 'immortal' stem, same act of clothing a body to make it divine/inviolable

support.locus: Sappho fr. 157 Voigt (recalled, not in local corpora)

cognate: Gk πότνια = Ved. pátnī < *pótnih₂; Gk Ἠώς = Ved. uṣás- < *h₂éwsōs
shared_syntax: the Dawn goddess's name with the title *pótnih₂ in the same clause (πότνια Ἠώς nom. ~ uṣā́ḥ ... pátnī nom.); Vedic adds a genitive of domain (svásarasya, bhúvanasya), a construction Greek also has with πότνια (πότνια θηρῶν)
context: HyAphr 223/230: Eos and Tithonus; RV 3.61.4: Uṣas goes forth, 'lady of the home/pasture'. In both the goddess is the personified Dawn. Weakness: πότνια is a stock epithet of many Greek goddesses and pátnī of several Vedic ones, and πότνια Ἠώς is not Homeric (GLAUx: only the two HyAphr lines), so chance is not excluded

cognate: Gk γλυκύς/γλυκερός = Lat. dulcis < *dl̥ku-/*dléwkus; Gk μέλι(τ-) = Lat. mel < *mélit
shared_syntax: 'sweet' + 'honey' as attribute pair (dulci melle ~ μέλιτι γλυκερῷ) and as comparative of sweetness against honey (melle dulci dulcior ~ μέλιτος γλυκίων)
context: Praise of something sweet (beloved, speech, mind, song) by honey: Plautus 'sweeter than sweet honey' to a lover; Lucretius 'touch with the sweet honey of the Muses'; Pindar's sweet mind surpassing the bees' labour; Homer's Nestor whose voice flowed sweeter than honey. Low: honey as the measure of sweetness is near-universal, so this is cognate wording but weak evidence of inheritance

note: All 268 bundles read. Most bundles (esp. Cato De agri cultura, Antiphon, Hippocratic and Old Russian partners) hold only shared common roots. Claims: dragon-slaying (Pindar/AVŚ), Father Sky (Gk/Ved/Lat), broad path > broad sea, clothing in the immortal, Lady Dawn, sweet honey. Considered and rejected: tecta domorum ~ στέγαι δόμων (generic), waking/sleeping merism (generic), πότνια μήτηρ ~ mātaraṃ ... patnīm (single Vedic apposition), λήξας ὕπνου ~ languet sopore (opposite sense), Νὺξ ἐρεβεννή ~ náktam ... rájobhiḥ (syntax differs), στεναγμῶν νέφος ~ stanáyan abhrā́ (metaphor vs literal).
